key_insight: Hybrid quantum PINNs used 38–44% fewer parameters but ran substantially slower than a classical PINN, showing that parameter count is not a reliable proxy for computational cost.
engineering_relevance: Benchmark wall-clock time across derivative and loss-gradient computations before choosing a quantum–classical architecture for physics-informed learning.
method: Evaluate a 1D seawater temperature diffusion benchmark with quantum circuits simulated on a CPU.
Compare a classical PINN, four hybrid configurations, and classical controls matched to the hybrids’ classical layers.
Time four cumulative stages: forward pass, first input gradient, second input gradient, and PDE-loss parameter gradient.
evidence_signal: Hybrids were 14–56× slower for forward passes and 10–97× slower for PDE-loss parameter gradients than the classical PINN; runtime increased approximately exponentially with qubit count over the tested range.
watch_item: Results concern a single benchmark with CPU-simulated circuits and should not be generalized directly to quantum hardware or other execution setups.
paper_title: Fewer Parameters, Longer Runtimes: The Wall-Clock Cost of Hybrid Quantum Physics-Informed Neural Networks
